cis_matches.control_title: Disable password authentication in favor of key-based SSH login
cis_matches.text: SSH should be configured to disable password authentication and require public-key authentication instead, reducing exposure to credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks. Combine this with disabling root login over SSH and restricting access to specific source networks where feasible.

raw_output: VULNERABLE: OpenSSH username enumeration via auth bailout timing. IDs: CVE:CVE-2018-15473

cve_records.text: OpenSSH through 7.7 is prone to a user enumeration vulnerability due to not delaying bailout for an invalid authenticating user until after the packet containing the request has been fully parsed, related to auth2-gss.c, auth2-hostbased.c, and auth2-pubkey.c.

raw_output: VULNERABLE: OpenSSH user enumeration via password-hash timing difference. IDs: CVE:CVE-2016-6210

cve_records.text: sshd in OpenSSH before 7.3, when SHA256 or SHA512 are used for user password hashing, uses BLOWFISH hashing on a static password when the username does not exist, which allows remote attackers to enumerate users by leveraging the timing difference between responses when a large password is provided.
